intent: Added 5 evenly spaced sensors with moderate size to improve line detection and steering precision. Chose balanced wheel track and radius for stability and speed. Expect improved line tracking, fewer line loss events, and stable steering.
rationale: Starting with a balanced and well-spaced sensor array to maximize line detection and steering precision. Using 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front of the robot to cover the tape width and some margin on each side, with a sensor size of 0.012 m to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track is set to 0.14 m for stability and maneuverability, with a moderate wheel radius of 0.035 m to balance speed and torque. The body width is 0.14 m to allow some tolerance for off-track limits without being too wide, and the body length is 0.18 m to keep the robot compact but stable. Mass is set to 0.8 kg to keep inertia manageable while allowing some robustness. The intent is to provide the integrator with a stable, well-sensed platform that can detect the line accurately and respond quickly to steering commands. Hypotheses include that the 5 sensors will provide sufficient resolution to detect line edges and curvature, and that the chosen body and wheel dimensions will balance speed and control. Measurement requests focus on completion, progress, line loss events, rms error, and steering oscillation to evaluate line tracking quality and stability.
